recipes.name: Baked Pasta with Sausage and Baby Portobello Mushroom White Sauce
ingredients_raw: 1 (8 ounce) package shredded whole milk mozzarella

steps.text: Preheat the oven's broiler and set the oven rack about 6 inches from the heat source.
Bring a large pot of lightly-salted water to a boil; cook the penne uncovered, stirring occasionally, until tender yet firm to the bite, about 11 minutes. Drain and return to the pot.

Meanwhile, heat 1 tablespoon of the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook and stir the sausage in the hot oil until crumbly and no longer pink, about 7 minutes: remove from the skillet, leaving the fat in the pan, and set aside. Pour the remaining 2 tablespoons of olive oil into the skillet and add the mushrooms and garlic. Cook and stir until the mushrooms have browned and begun to release their liquid, about 5 minutes more. Return the sausage to the skillet and pour in the heavy cream. Season with salt and pepper and return to a simmer, cooking until the sauce begins to thicken, about 5 minutes more. Pour the sauce over the pasta and stir. Stir in 1/2 cup mozzarella and Parmesan. Pour into a 9x13-inch baking dish and sprinkle with remaining 1/2 cup mozzarella cheese.
Broil in the preheated oven until the mozzarella cheese is bubbly and golden brown, 5 to 7 minutes.

raw_recipe.description: Cremini mushrooms (also called 'Baby Portobellos') join Italian sausage in this hot and bubbly pasta.

review.reviewBody: Fantastic! Thank you so much for enhancing my repertoire of pasta dishes!! My family loved this and hubby went back for seconds... raving about how delicious it is! And for those who don't have heavy cream in the house... I used 2% milk, added about 1/2 cup of butter and some flour and it was thick and creamy and tasted fab! A winner!!!

I made this with some modifications to make it healthier. I used high fiber penne pasta instead of regular pasta. I cooked this with hot Italian sausage with one medium onion cut up to give it an extra kick. Once those were cooked I drained the fat, added three cups of fresh spinach and one small container of baby tomatoes sliced. I reduced the heavy whipping cream to 1/2 cup, added 2 tables of butter, 1 1/4 C of chicken stock and 2 tablespoons of flour. Very delicious without all of the unwanted fat!

Excellent! But it needs a few tweaks. First instructions say to heat the broiler and cook the pasta. It took me a lot longer than 15 minutes to make the dish, so I had to turn off my broiler for a while and the pasta was cold and stuck together before I needed it. I would do those tasks later in the recipe. Recipe says to pour in (cold) cream and simmer about 5 minutes until thickened. My cream wasn't even warm after 5 minutes...needed a lot more time to simmer and thicken. Mine never did thicken, so I added a cornstarch slurry. My training is to always add the garlic near the end, so I added it when the mushrooms were almost done. The sauce tasted BLAND!!! Added extra S&P, Italian seasoning, white wine, and oodles of fresh basil - still VERY bland. Added extra Mozzarella both in and on top, using about 3/4 c each., about 12-16 oz. total. The sauce still tasted bland, BUT the final dish was wonderful!! Agree with adding extra cream or broth, i.e. 2 cups. Topping of broiled Mozzarella cheese was wonderful! (I thought it was going to need bread crumbs, but it didn't.) Total cooking time was closer to about 35 minutes for me. The final dish was tasty, creamy, and wonderful! Thanks for the recipe!
Easy to make and delicious. The measurements are spot on. I changed the servings to 4 and added a tablespoon of tomato sauce for color and flavor. It was perfect!

The earthy flavor of the cremini mushrooms really stands out in this dish. I used rotini instead of penne (personal preference). I cut back the amount of pasta a bit and increased the cream to almost 2 cups. Was concerned it might be too dry otherwise. Like another reviewer I didn't use oil to cook the sausage, just for the mushrooms and garlic. I don't have a broiler proof baking dish so I baked it at 375 degrees for 25 minutes until bubbly. Hubby says it's a keeper.

This was really hearty and made great leftovers. I would suggest draining and rinsing the sausage before returning it to the pan though. Between the sausage and the Parmesan it can become greasy. I topped it with panko added to the cheese mixture and broiled it at the end for a lovely crisp top. My guys are fans!

My husband thought this was fantastic. I made a few modifications to make it a little healthier. I used whole wheat penne. I cooked the 16 oz box the recipe called for but when I started to add the other ingredients to the pasta it looked like there was just too much pasta for the amount of sauce. I only used about 3/4 of the pasta. I didn't use any additional olive oil as called for in the recipe. I browned the sausage with no extra oil. I used the grease from the sausage to cook the mushrooms and garlic without adding extra oil. I also added a cup or so of chopped fresh spinach to the mixture. This was really good. I will definitely make it again .
This was so simple and tasty! I followed the recipe to a "T" only I added some parm. cheese to the cream in the skillet to make a nice alfredo sauce. It was delicious!

Scrumptious! I mostly followed the recipe with the following calorie-cutting variations: less pasta, a can of evaporated milk instead of the heavy cream, reduced fat mozzarella, and a chopped bell pepper added along with the mushrooms and garlic. This is a definite keeper for the "quick and hearty meal" category!

Good basis for a meal but I drained the grease and sauté onions,zucchini, garlic added fresh peeled tomatoes and a splash of white wine and fresh basil. Tasted great and good for lunch leftovers to reheat at work the next day. Green salad and a slice of fresh french bread made it a yummy meal.

This is a FANTASTIC dish! I made a big change because I am LAZY (and 76 years old). I did a no-bake! I cooked the pasta al dente and set aside. Then I mixed all the other ingredients in a skillet and cooked over med-hi heat into a fragrant sauce. Then I gave everyone a bowl and told them to mix their own stuff. Everyone loved it!!!
This dish was better than expected! It was an easy recipe to follow and can be made ahead. I halved everything but it would be great if serving a crowd.
Totally hated it. Very bland.

I made it yesterday for dinner at the first time. I cooked it for two , so I had to reduce the ingredients. We loved it. I had to make the Italian Sausage by myself, because I live in a very little german town with only two small grocery stores. I will definetly make it again. Please apologize my english writing.
This is delicious. Followed the recipe just halved it, but still used 8 ounces of mozzarella.

Have made twice now, first time followed exactly. This makes a lot and was bit on the dry side. Second time I made using only 12 oz pasta and added I/2 pd more mushrooms also used hot Italian sausage it was more creamy and not so dry.
Made it exactly according to recipe. It's not a colorful dish but it is delicious! I've already made it a second time and just found the recipe a month ago. Definitely making again and again
Delicious!! - I substituted the bulk Italian sausage and used spicy turkey italian sausage. Perfect quick weekday meal.
really delicious
Loved the flavor, but my sauce never thickened.
